s1.syndrome_frame: Neonatal oral masses causing feeding difficulties
salient_findings: Multiple masses protruding from the gums
Six round, soft, pedunculated swellings on the maxillary and mandibular anterior alveolar ridges
key_facts: Born at 38 weeks of gestation via cesarean section
No family history of hereditary disease
Six masses: two on the maxillary anterior alveolar ridge and four on the mandibular anterior alveolar ridge
Lesions were well defined, firm, smooth, and pink
Infant unable to close her mouth completely

shortlist.label: Congenital epulis
shortlist.why_kept: Multiple masses protruding from gums, interfering with feeding, in a newborn

shortlist.label: Congenital granular cell tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Similar presentation to congenital epulis, with masses on the alveolar ridge

shortlist.label: Melanotic neuroectodermal tumor of infancy
shortlist.why_kept: Rare tumor that can present as oral masses in infancy

shortlist.label: Gingival cyst of the newborn
shortlist.why_kept: Common oral lesion in newborns, can cause feeding difficulties

shortlist.label: Myofibroma
shortlist.why_kept: Can present as a congenital oral mass, although less common than other options

raw.rationale: The presence of multiple, well-defined, firm, smooth, and pink masses protruding from the gums in a newborn, particularly on the alveolar ridges, is most consistent with congenital epulis, which are rare, benign tumors that typically occur on the gums of newborns.

rejected.label: Congenital granular cell tumor
rejected.why: While possible, congenital granular cell tumors are less common and typically present with a single lesion, not multiple masses as described in this case.

rejected.label: Melanotic neuroectodermal tumor of infancy
rejected.why: This tumor usually presents with a single, pigmented lesion, which does not match the description of the masses in this case.

rejected.label: Gingival cyst of the newborn
rejected.why: Gingival cysts of the newborn are typically small, solitary, and not as large or numerous as the masses described.

rejected.label: Myofibroma
rejected.why: Myofibromas can occur in the oral cavity but are not typically characterized by multiple, pedunculated masses on the gums as seen in this case.
